or the work being assessed. Retain the observed extent, interruption and
conclusion in its outcome and evidence. The legal pairs are:

| Performance | Permitted verdicts | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `performed` | Any of the five verdicts | Evidence establishes that the evaluation was undertaken, including a scoped basis or capability diagnosis. Its extent and conclusion remain separate facts. |
| `not_performed` | Any except `satisfied`, with the evidence condition below | Evidence establishes that the evaluation was not undertaken. Dispatch or admission alone does not establish performance. |
| `unconfirmed` | Any except `satisfied`, with the evidence condition below | Whether the evaluation was undertaken is not established. |

An interruption does not erase evaluation already undertaken or admissible
evidence obtained. A suite aborted after a witnessed failure is performed with
that partial extent and falsifies “all tests pass”. A completed load test that
cannot generate its required load is performed but indeterminate on the
requested service-performance predicate. Neither case is a never-run test.
Satisfaction still requires all evidence and completion conditions selected by
the predicate's evaluation rule; performed alone proves none of them.

When the selected evaluation was not undertaken or its performance is
unconfirmed, separately admissible counterevidence to its bound predicate can
still establish falsified; an established basis or scope diagnosis can likewise
establish invalid_basis or out_of_frame. The result identifies that independent
support without inventing execution. Without deciding support it is
indeterminate. An absent return establishes neither non-performance nor an
undecidable evaluation: retain the missing slot and what is actually known.

A missing required judgment stays an absent coverage slot, with the known
performance fact or its uncertainty; it is not a fabricated child result. A
performed but undecidable evaluation differs from a known unperformed one and
from unconfirmed execution. A failed admission check can conclude while
downstream work does not. The plan fixes which predicates are required; a
precondition is evidence for its dependent evaluation unless the plan separately
requires that precondition as a predicate. A concluding basis/scope diagnosis
on P reports invalid_basis/out_of_frame on P with its supporting evidence; a
different admission predicate is not silently substituted for P. An aborted
procedure does not erase separately authenticated counterexamples observed
during the attempt. Every result projection preserves these
coordinates and the original predicate; a verdict alone is an insufficient
handoff where performance is material.

An effect observation is `not_requested`, `not_started`, `completed`, `partial`,
`reverted` or `unknown`, on its declared observation boundary. These values describe the selected effect and observation
boundary, not the predicate verdict. `not_started` needs evidence that the selected effect did not begin, including
an authenticated rejection before mutation. Transport dispatch alone proves
neither effect completion nor absence; `unknown` includes a lost acknowledgment
after possible execution.
`reverted` means that at least one part began and every begun part is observed to have been reversed within
the declared boundary, with the reversal and any unstarted remainder retained
as evidence. For every effect value, the boundary includes each material part
the operation may have affected under its supported operating model and any
observed departure, whether requested or unintended. Irreversible messages or
other material external effects cannot be omitted to improve a result.
`partial` means an observed
completed part and an observed requested but unexecuted, or reverted, remainder.
If any material remainder has unknown completion, the state is `unknown`,
retaining the completed parts as evidence. An effect can be completed while
the intended product outcome is falsified.
An empty local log or discarded context does not establish no effect.
`not_requested` states an established effect-free scope under that operating
model; lack of a request alone is insufficient. A material possible unintended
effect without sufficient observation is `unknown`. If observation establishes
that an unrequested possible part did not begin, it contributes `not_requested`
at this boundary, retaining that observation and any earlier uncertainty.
It is not an uncompleted requested remainder. A requested part observed not to
begin remains `not_started`.

A refined value is the pair of original domain outcome and cause in its
declared reason domain, including an explicit missing-reason case. A domain
refinement preserves that qualified original outcome and supplies a
total, reason-sensitive map into this record. If the original outcome is too
coarse to determine a verdict, its required reason distinguishes the cases; a
consumer cannot guess from a word such as `refused`, `ready` or `accepted`.
A missing required reason maps the claimed predicate to indeterminate and
leaves that contribution inadmissible as deciding support for its slot;
retain its raw outcome and unresolved authentication. Its claimed predicate
remains indeterminate until admissible evidence decides it. Independently
established counterevidence or a basis/scope diagnosis uses the legal pairs above
on that same bound predicate; it does not invent execution or completion.
Requested or material possible unintended effects without sufficient observation
are unknown, never defaulted to not_requested. Unconfirmed evaluation performance
stays unconfirmed. Domain meaning stays with its domain owner.
No refinement turns failure, undecidability, non-performance or unknown effect
completion into greater standing. A new result over a different predicate does
not overwrite the earlier result.

Candidate availability, candidate fitness and authorised acceptance are three
predicates. `candidate_ready` can satisfy availability while fitness remains
falsified or unassessed. A lawful yield can satisfy the selected yielding
contract while product completion remains unresolved. A decision result binds
the predicate “disposition D on subject S at basis B was made under mandate M
by its bound authority”. A lawful rejection can satisfy that predicate while
candidate fitness remains undecided. Recording the decision is not its authority.
A not-applicable classification needs a supported applicability judgment; it is
never a synonym for a missing evaluation.

A stop reports the actual destination or task predicate through this record,
with its reason, observed effects and outstanding obligations. Its verdict
is indeterminate when the outcome remains undecided, falsified when admissible
evidence defeats that predicate, or the established scope/basis diagnosis.
Lawfulness of stopping is a separate decision predicate.

## Result conjunction

Conjunction evaluates whether all required predicates and their material joins
hold on the declared composite subject and basis. It retains the contributing
results, their authentication and predicate mapping, known failures and their
citations, uncovered required coverage, uncertain effects and invalidators.
The aggregate is another result in the same algebra, with those components
available through sufficient references. Its summary never replaces them.

The required set comes from the composite's applicability and coverage
contract, not from the list of returns received. F4's preservation obligation
therefore makes a missing required return visible even when every available
return is satisfied. F2/F6 also retain an authenticated counterexample when
another slot is missing. Frame conjunction and the library's Conjoin operation
apply this same distinction; their owners supply which predicates and joins
are required, not another rule for erasing failures or filling gaps.

The aggregate evaluation has performance performed when its combining rule is
applied; this does not change component performance. The composite declares its
effect boundary and the selected effect parts within it. First resolve a current
observation for each part, retaining the contributing observations, identities,
ordering and any supported supersession. A later timestamp alone is no
supersession argument. Conflicting or insufficient observations leave the part
unknown. Normalize every material possibly affected part, including one owned
by an absent evaluation slot, through the effect-observation rule in
[Result algebra](#result-algebra). That rule distinguishes a requested part
that did not start from an unrequested possible part observed not to begin.
The composite supplies no different classification for either case.

Sequential stages can affect the same part. Their local completion labels are
not inputs to the composite join until mapped onto that part's observed state
at the composite boundary. A completed deployment followed by its completed
rollback is reverted for the deployment effect; a subsequent completed
reapplication is completed there. The historical rollback remains evidence.
The declarations retain every material external part, including irreversible
ones; a local reversal cannot silently remove them from the scope.

Over the resulting disjoint part observations: any unknown gives unknown;
all not_requested gives not_requested; completed with only completed or
not_requested gives completed; not_started with only not_started or
not_requested gives not_started; reverted with only reverted, not_started or
not_requested gives reverted; every remaining fully observed mixture gives
partial. Retain each observation's part and contributing components. The combining
operation's own lack of mutation cannot label an effectful composite not_requested.

First authenticate each contribution against its producer, subject, basis and
required plan membership. An unauthenticated claim cannot discharge an
obligation. A missing planned judgment remains an absent slot with its known performance
fact or uncertainty; required coverage outside an authenticated plan remains
uncovered. These are separate
conditions. An invalid contribution does not erase an independently
authenticated finding.

For an interpretable composite predicate and governing basis:

1. Any authenticated, applicable falsification of a required predicate or material join makes
   the conjunction `falsified`. Missing or undecidable other coverage remains
   explicit alongside it.
2. With no such falsification, an invalid required basis prevents satisfaction
   and yields `invalid_basis`; a required out-of-frame judgment yields
   `out_of_frame` when no invalid basis applies.
3. Otherwise any unresolved applicability, missing evaluation, undecidable
   predicate or undecided material join yields `indeterminate`.
4. `satisfied` requires every applicable obligation and material join to be
   authentically satisfied, with coverage itself established. An empty list
   proves nothing unless the declared required set is established as empty.

The composite declaration distinguishes its admission conditions from the
material joins of the predicate being evaluated. Each relation has one of
those roles in that evaluation. A failed admission condition prevents an
interpretation; a false required join is counterevidence within an admitted
interpretation. The result names that declared role instead of reclassifying a
known failed join as a missing basis. If the composite subject or governing basis itself cannot be interpreted, the
aggregate is `invalid_basis`; independently valid component failures and their
scope remain exposed. This does not pronounce them false or forgotten.
Effect uncertainty prevents satisfaction where the predicate requires a known
effect state. An unrelated effect does not automatically invalidate a different
predicate; the dependency relation must justify its relevance.

A declared operator states its truth and falsity conditions over exact leaf
predicates and joins. On its fully decided admitted domain, those conditions
are disjoint and exhaustive, including failure of a required join. An
overlapping, incomplete or uninterpretable operator declaration is invalid_basis.
Unresolved well-formedness makes the operator result indeterminate and supplies
neither satisfaction nor falsification; independently valid leaf results remain
visible. Once well-formedness is established, its result can be satisfied only when authenticated
evidence establishes its truth condition and the material joins and coverage
needed for that condition. It can be falsified only on an established falsity
condition. Otherwise a material invalid_basis yields invalid_basis, a material
out_of_frame yields out_of_frame when no invalid basis applies, and every
remaining undecided case is indeterminate. Only dependencies needed to decide
the bound predicate enter that ordering. Authentication, original failure
retention, performance and effect composition remain the rules above. Negation
or disjunction evaluates a different predicate; it cannot erase a failed leaf
or pass that result off as conjunction of all leaves. A first-nonfailure rule
cannot turn an undecided fallback into success.

Sequential composition records an unreturned dependent evaluation as an absent
slot, retaining its observed performance, extent and missing conclusion. A lawful regrouping requires the same interpretable composite basis, required
leaf predicates, joins, normalized effect parts and authentication, with no intermediate basis failure
hidden by the grouping. On that fixed domain, retained component sets combine
by union, the conjunction precedence is associative, and the effect join over
normalized disjoint parts is associative. The argument is mathematical: union
retains the same authenticated leaves under either grouping; selecting the
highest applicable diagnostic in the declared precedence over those leaves
has the same result. Normalized disjoint effect observations likewise retain
the same parts, so the stated unknown and completion conditions decide the same
aggregate. An intermediate result must retain those leaves and parts; a bare
verdict cannot establish this equivalence. This grants no associativity to an
arbitrary declared operator; regrouping it requires preservation of the same
outer predicate and its own demonstrated associativity law. An invalid
intermediate join is a failed premise of that rewrite, not evidence that every
arbitrary grouping is equivalent. Reordering
operations additionally needs an effect-independence law; associativity alone
supplies no such permission.

Sequential operations compose under their applicable owning contracts:
[UP-016/017](DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md#transformation-admission-completeness-stdo-up-016)
for design composition and [AC-016](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-016-typed-composition)
within a_c. Their returned result applies the operator rule above to the
declared outer predicate using
its preservation argument and the retained component results. For a pipeline
whose contract requires every stage postcondition, this is the conjunction
above; a recovery path need not require a failed earlier test to become true.
Unexecuted stages remain coverage facts, with no invented evaluations. A
sequence without an established outer interpretation or join returns the
applicable unresolved or invalid-basis result rather than a guessed success.

1010	### Conjunction of results
1011	
1012	Conjunction combines results into one result for a composite predicate: a
1013	claim made of component claims, a decision over several evaluations, or
1014	the outer contract of composed steps. It is defined here once, over the
1015	core. A member or profile that combines results applies this rule and
1016	declares only the choices it leaves open (P4a, P4b, P5, P6). Purpose and
1017	material relation: failure, undecidability, non-performance and uncertain
1018	effects stay distinct after combination, so a composite can neither report
1019	success nor hide which kind of gap it has while one of them remains in
1020	what it requires.
1021	
1022	A conjunction takes three inputs and keeps them apart:
1023	
1024	1. the closed results returned, each a core value with its predicate and
1025	   domain outcome;
1026	2. the planned assessments that have no closed result applicable to the
1027	   composite: evaluations the composite requires that were not performed,
1028	   or whose result is absent, stale, bound to another subject or basis, or
1029	   incapable of establishing its claim;
1030	3. the required coverage that no planned assessment addresses: for a
1031	   required obligation set R and the coverage C that the planned
1032	   assessments admit, the uncovered coverage R minus C.
1033	
1034	Gaps. A conjunction with any item in the second or third input is never
1035	`satisfied`. Its record names which kind of gap it has, not performed,
1036	uncovered or both, and each item. An uncovered obligation is never
1037	reported as satisfied or as an omitted planned assessment; a planned
1038	assessment without a closed result is never reported as uncovered or as an
1039	`indeterminate` component.
1040	
1041	Stale results. A held result is stale for a composite when the basis it
1042	binds is not the basis the composite requires of that component, because
1043	a later state has superseded or advanced it or because it binds another
1044	subject or basis (§2, Basis). Two questions stay apart, so that one
1045	composite has one reported value (P3, P5, P6):
1046	
1047	- an evaluation performed on a subject or basis that is stale, advanced,
1048	  ambiguous or mismatched against the one it must bind returns
1049	  `invalid_basis` for its own predicate, or is reactivated on the current
1050	  basis; [RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates)
1051	  states this law over frames, and a conjunction that receives that
1052	  `invalid_basis` holds it as a returned result;
1053	- a component whose only held result is stale has no closed result
1054	  applicable to the composite: on the basis the composite requires, its
1055	  evaluation was not performed. It is a planned assessment without a
1056	  closed result, in the second input, and a gap. Its stale value is
1057	  neither counted as a returned result nor relabelled `invalid_basis` for
1058	  the composite, and it stays in the record with its own basis;
1059	- the declared basis relations disagree (Reported value below) only among
1060	  returned results, each bound to the basis the composite requires of it,
1061	  whose bases the declared rule requires to agree or to join in a coherent
1062	  composite basis, and which do not.
1063	
1064	A stale `satisfied` never counts toward the composite. Purpose and
1065	material relation: answering one stale component as a gap in one place and
1066	as `invalid_basis` in another would give one composite two reported
1067	values; keeping the evaluation's own value apart from the composite's gap
1068	keeps the reported value unique and the stale result visible.
1069	
1070	Survival. Every known failure (a `falsified` result with its
1071	counterexample), every planned assessment without a closed result and
1072	every uncovered obligation is carried with the composite and survives every
1073	join: combining conjunctions takes the union of known failures and of
1074	planned assessments without a closed result, and recomputes uncovered
1075	coverage over the combined obligations. A known failure and a gap of
1076	either kind survive every join. Common agreement among contributors
1077	cannot discard a constraint or a material counterexample that only one
1078	contributor found. A missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate

1090	relations agree, and the second and third inputs are empty. A composite

### Results

Every performed evaluation returns one value of the core result algebra,
directly or as a refined value mapped into it (P5):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `satisfied` | the declared predicate holds on the exact basis |
| `falsified` | a declared counterexample defeats it |
| `indeterminate` | the available admissible evidence cannot decide it |
| `out_of_frame` | the evaluation requires an undeclared material relation or capability |
| `invalid_basis` | the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation |

This core is the only one. Results of constraints, judgments, frame
evaluations, stops, work steps and effects are stated in it or in a
refinement mapped into it, so that results from any members combine under
one rule ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)). Purpose and
material relation: no combination can report success while a failure, an
undecided question, an unperformed evaluation or an uncertain effect
remains, and none of these can be mistaken for another (P5, P6).

Recording. A result records its core value together with the predicate
evaluated and the original domain outcome, which is the refined value
where a refinement produced it. A mapping into the core never owns domain
meaning: the member, profile or adopting Product that defines the refined
value keeps it, and a consumer that needs the domain distinction reads the
domain outcome, never the core value alone (P1, P6).

Standing. The standing of a result is what it establishes about its
predicate; it is distinct from the standing of a commitment (§1). Only
`satisfied` establishes the predicate. `falsified` establishes that the
predicate fails and names the counterexample. `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` establish neither, and each names what
would decide: the evidence, the missing relation or capability with its
owner where the subject gives one, or the basis repair. By support for the
predicate, `satisfied` stands above each other value, and the other four
are not ordered among themselves.

No refinement or mapping raises a result's standing (P5, P6):

- a falsified or failed result never maps to a satisfied or successful one;
- a result that admissible evidence cannot decide never maps to
  `satisfied`;
- an evaluation that was not performed stays distinct from one whose
  evidence cannot decide: it has no
  [closed result](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), and it is never mapped
  to `indeterminate` or to any other core value;
- an effect whose completion is unknown never maps to no effect or to
  completed.

Not performed. An evaluation that is required or planned and was not
performed has no closed result; an actor cannot report an evaluation it
did not perform (P6). Nothing is coerced to success: a failed,
indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope or invalid-basis result follows
the declared result algebra and returns its own value under it, never
`satisfied`, and a missing result, being no result, enters every
conjunction over it as a gap: a planned assessment without a closed result
where an assessment was planned, and uncovered coverage where none was.
This
conserves
[RF-012](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-012-closed-results),
whose five values the table restates unchanged, and
[AC-007](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal),
whose rule that a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or
invalid-basis result follows the declared algebra rather than being
coerced to success is the sentence before; both are restated here once.
[REFERENCE_FRAME §3](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-012-closed-results) states
RF-012 as a law over frames and
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal)
states AC-007 as a law over constraints; each uses this core and neither
defines it again.

Refinements. A member, profile or adopting Product that needs finer
outcomes defines a refinement. The refinement names the question it
answers and the predicate its mapping is for, and maps every refined value
to exactly one core value. No outcome exists outside the core; a
refinement adds no core value and keeps the pressure of `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` explicit. Where a refined value would
map to one of two core values according to its cause, the cause is part of
the refined value and each resulting value maps once (P5, P1). A further
refinement, by a member, profile, project or adopting Product, may split a
refined value by cause. The parent-value rule governs every such split:
each child value names its parent value and its cause and keeps its
parent's core value; a child that needs a different core value needs a
different parent value, which only the owner of the parent declares; and
no child takes `satisfied` from a parent that is not `satisfied`. No
further refinement raises a result's standing (P5, P6, P1). Purpose and
material relation: a consumer that reads a parent value reads the same
core value from each of its children, so a split by cause adds a domain
distinction and never changes what the parent establishes (P5, P6). The
refinements for admission, activation and steps are
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition); each other
member, profile and adopting Product states its mapping where it defines
its values.

Availability, assessment and acceptance are separate results, each with its
own predicate: that a step produced a candidate; that the candidate meets
its declared criteria; and that the
[decision owner](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation) accepts it at its
boundary. A step having produced a candidate never maps to the candidate's
fitness or acceptance, and acceptance is never inferred from a successful
step (P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition),
[EVALUATION §4](EVALUATION.md#4-review-results) and
[§5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance)).

Out of frame or indeterminate. The boundary between these values is drawn
on what the activated frame declares and on what the step did with it (P5,
finite capacity and graceful total handling; the material relation drawn
is the three-way out_of_frame boundary: capability not declared, capability
declared and exercised, capability declared and not exercised; rc.2 RF
#rf-012-closed-results). Three cases; the first two name core values, and
the third names none:

- `out_of_frame` when the claim requires a material relation or an
  evaluator capability that the activated frame does not declare. The
  result names the missing relation or capability, its owner where the
  subject gives one, and the reconfiguration pressure it creates
  ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement); rc.2 RF
  #reconfigure-when-necessary). A term the claim depends on and the frame
  leaves undefined is an undeclared material relation: its meaning can
  alter the result and it enters through no declared input (rc.2 RF
  #material-relation, RF-003; P1). Whether the step exercised anything is
  irrelevant to this value; the ground is the missing declaration.
- `indeterminate` when the available admissible evidence cannot decide the
  claim (rc.2 RF-012). The result names the evidence that would decide, as
  its residual uncertainty (rc.2 RF #return-a-closed-result). Where the
  claim also depends on an undeclared relation or capability,
  `out_of_frame` and `indeterminate` each have a lawful ground; the result
  names the value it returns and that ground, and this boundary excludes
  neither (P5).
- no value of its own when the step did not exercise a declared capability
  the evaluation requires. A result is returned wherever a sufficient
  evaluation or an applicable judgment exists without that capability,
  identifying its evidence, verdict and residual uncertainty like any
  closed result (rc.2 RF #rf-012-closed-results, #return-a-closed-result):
  a counterexample found by what was exercised, as when source inspection
  falsifies A in a claim of A and B, returns `falsified`, and common
  agreement cannot discard it (rc.2 RF #result-conjunction). Where none
  exists because the capability was not exercised, the evaluation was not
  performed and has no result: the step's stop state carries it,
  `incomplete` under
  [construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability), and
  its work state ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart))
  carries the unexercised capability as a residual (P6). In either case
  the unexercised part, B above, has no result: in every conjunction over
  it, it is a planned assessment without a closed result, and the known
  failure A survives with it ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)).
  The evaluation's result and the step's stop state answer different
  questions, so the step's stop value never becomes the evaluation's
  result.

Foundation to law for results and their combination (family F3). The
table covers every rule of §4 and the result grounds of §2 Imports
between members, in the format of
[Foundation to law](#foundation-to-law), which states the standing of its
consequences. Purpose and material relation: a reader of §4 sees which
commitments each result rule rests on and which choices it adds, with their
owners (P6, P2). Instance premises, which the commitments do not supply:
(i) an evaluation declares its predicate, subject and basis; (ii) results
of several evaluations, steps or members are combined into one decision;
(iii) members, profiles and adopting Products need outcomes finer than the
core.

| P5 (derived from P0 and P6), P6 (independent); (i), (ii) | every performed evaluation returns one closed value of one algebra shared by every member, with a value for a claim that holds, one that fails, one the evidence cannot decide, one that needs a relation or capability the frame lacks, and one whose basis cannot support it | [Results](#results), the value table | the value names, and the division of P5's outcomes other than success into `indeterminate`, `out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis`, conserved from RF-012; owner: this section | 3, 9 |

### Conjunction of results

Conjunction combines results into one result for a composite predicate: a
claim made of component claims, a decision over several evaluations, or
the outer contract of composed steps. It is defined here once, over the
core. A member or profile that combines results applies this rule and
declares only the choices it leaves open (P4a, P4b, P5, P6). Purpose and
material relation: failure, undecidability, non-performance and uncertain
effects stay distinct after combination, so a composite can neither report
success nor hide which kind of gap it has while one of them remains in
what it requires.

A conjunction takes three inputs and keeps them apart:

1. the closed results returned, each a core value with its predicate and
   domain outcome;
2. the planned assessments that have no closed result applicable to the
   composite: evaluations the composite requires that were not performed,
   or whose result is absent, stale, bound to another subject or basis, or
   incapable of establishing its claim;
3. the required coverage that no planned assessment addresses: for a
   required obligation set R and the coverage C that the planned
   assessments admit, the uncovered coverage R minus C.

Gaps. A conjunction with any item in the second or third input is never
`satisfied`. Its record names which kind of gap it has, not performed,
uncovered or both, and each item. An uncovered obligation is never
reported as satisfied or as an omitted planned assessment; a planned
assessment without a closed result is never reported as uncovered or as an
`indeterminate` component.

Stale results. A held result is stale for a composite when the basis it
binds is not the basis the composite requires of that component, because
a later state has superseded or advanced it or because it binds another
subject or basis (§2, Basis). Two questions stay apart, so that one
composite has one reported value (P3, P5, P6):

- an evaluation performed on a subject or basis that is stale, advanced,
  ambiguous or mismatched against the one it must bind returns
  `invalid_basis` for its own predicate, or is reactivated on the current
  basis; [RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates)
  states this law over frames, and a conjunction that receives that
  `invalid_basis` holds it as a returned result;
- a component whose only held result is stale has no closed result
  applicable to the composite: on the basis the composite requires, its
  evaluation was not performed. It is a planned assessment without a
  closed result, in the second input, and a gap. Its stale value is
  neither counted as a returned result nor relabelled `invalid_basis` for
  the composite, and it stays in the record with its own basis;
- the declared basis relations disagree (Reported value below) only among
  returned results, each bound to the basis the composite requires of it,
  whose bases the declared rule requires to agree or to join in a coherent
  composite basis, and which do not.

A stale `satisfied` never counts toward the composite. Purpose and
material relation: answering one stale component as a gap in one place and
as `invalid_basis` in another would give one composite two reported
values; keeping the evaluation's own value apart from the composite's gap
keeps the reported value unique and the stale result visible.

Survival. Every known failure (a `falsified` result with its
counterexample), every planned assessment without a closed result and
every uncovered obligation is carried with the composite and survives every
join: combining conjunctions takes the union of known failures and of
planned assessments without a closed result, and recomputes uncovered
coverage over the combined obligations. A known failure and a gap of
either kind survive every join. Common agreement among contributors
cannot discard a constraint or a material counterexample that only one
contributor found. A missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate
mandatory result stays unresolved under the declared rule, and aggregate
satisfied status cannot replace it (P4b, P5).

Predicates travel. Each component keeps its predicate and domain outcome
through every join, so an uncertain effect stays distinct from a failure
and from an undecided claim, and a `satisfied` for one predicate never
counts toward another: a step's `satisfied` for "a candidate is available"
never counts toward the candidate's fitness or acceptance.

Reported value. The conjunction is `satisfied` only when every mandatory
result is `satisfied` with valid applicable evidence, the declared basis
relations agree, and the second and third inputs are empty. A composite
with a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint or an uncovered
required obligation cannot project success. Where a mandatory result is
not `satisfied`, the conjunction
reports a non-satisfied value chosen by its declared rule from those
returned; no universal order among the non-satisfied values exists, and
the member or profile that applies the conjunction declares its own in
its declared rule. Where every mandatory returned result is `satisfied`
and the declared basis relations disagree, the conjunction reports
`invalid_basis`, because no coherent composite basis supports the
composite predicate (§2, Basis); any gaps stay recorded by kind. Where
every mandatory returned result is `satisfied`, the declared basis
relations agree and a gap remains, the conjunction reports
`indeterminate`, because the results it holds cannot decide the composite
predicate; that value is the conjunction's own, and the gaps stay
recorded by kind. A `falsified` result that is not mandatory stays in the
conjunction's record with its predicate and is never discarded. Where
every mandatory result is `satisfied`, the declared basis relations agree
and no gap remains, a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint
falsifies the conjunction whichever contributor found it, and without one
the conjunction's value is the one its declared rule gives over the
mandatory results.

The declared rule. A conjunction declares which results are mandatory; how
conflict and indeterminacy are handled; which basis relations must agree,
results on different bases combining only under a declared coherent
composite basis (§2, Basis); which decision authority owns the
conjunction; how results that are not mandatory count; and whether any
result may veto or defer the decision.
Conjunction does not transfer the semantic authority of a contributing
evaluation (P6, P4a).

Composition of results. The result of composed steps for the outer
predicate is the conjunction of the steps' results, with the outer
contract's obligations as the required coverage. That each step returned
`satisfied` supports the outer predicate only where the refinement's
premises hold ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement),
Refinement).

Provenance: rc.2 RF #result-conjunction and
#applicability-and-required-results, and the combination rule of
conservation accounting.

required judgment and owner ruling is present and applicable; and no active
non-closure condition remains. A mandatory obligation whose applicability is
unknown, or whose evidence is insufficient, withholds the dependent claim;
evidence presence alone is not satisfaction. The existing owner decides any
reserved acceptance (P6, P5; rc.2 #condition-based-closure-and-reuse).

[conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results) with the
declared obligations as required coverage. This section owns the

states in Recording a result without review, with the ticket as the
existing carrier. The conditions that still apply include sprint-close
law (§3) and the design profile's law (P6, P2).

and O under the reuse rule of

581	## Construction assurance
582	
583	An assurance consumer binds the selected obligation, interpreted predicate,
584	subject, governing basis, assumptions and admissible evidence. Apply the
585	subrelations below at the decision that relies on them: preservation at a
586	construction join, assertion and observation justification at evaluation,
587	dependence and risk at evidence selection, and applicability at change or reuse.
588	The consumer supplies its domain policy and required assurance; these shared
589	relations create no additional evaluation stage, role, record or authority.
590	Every conclusion uses the [result algebra](#result-algebra), and required
591	predicates combine under [result conjunction](#result-conjunction).
592	
593	### Preservation obligations
594	
595	For a selected construction from A toward Z, bind governing assumptions Gamma,
596	state or trace domains X_i, transition relations F_i contained in
597	X_i × X_(i+1), and properties P_i to retain or establish at each boundary.
598	Required effects and trace properties belong to the outcome predicate where
599	material. The obligation for a claimed step is:
600	
601	```text
602	For every x and x':
603	  P_i(x) and F_i(x, x') implies P_(i+1)(x').
604	```
605	
606	Establish the initial condition, each step's applicable premises and the
607	composition boundaries before using the steps as an end-to-end argument. A
608	preceding postcondition must establish the next precondition; otherwise acquire
609	and justify the missing condition. Establish that the final property implies
610	Z. Supported local claims remain usable when a required join or final implication
611	is unresolved, but they do not establish that outer claim. For an invariant,
612	induction requires its initial case and preservation on every admitted step;
613	neither an invariant nor repeated execution proves progress or termination.
614	
615	The relation covers every outcome, effect and assumption material to the claim.
616	A successful-completion relation alone says nothing about refusal, failure,
617	interruption or unknown effects. Their handling retains the result and recovery
618	contracts. The actual execution's conformance to the relation is a separate
619	claim. Concurrency, alternative branches and external effects require their
620	applicable composition law; a sequential argument supplies none automatically.
621	The library's [Composition law](TRANSFORMATION_LIBRARY.md#composition-law) binds
622	these obligations to the selected operation and its material joins.
623	
624	Exact transformations preserve the declared meaning. An approximation declares
625	its adequacy relation and establishes a bound for the whole composition; local
626	tolerances do not establish that bound by themselves. Across algorithmic,
627	informational and computational accounts, identify the maps and what they
628	preserve under [Orthogonal descriptions](#orthogonal-descriptions). A formula
629	states an obligation; a mathematical argument, structural check, finite model,
630	sampled test and observed execution retain their distinct subjects and reach.
631	Unproved universal claims remain unresolved. They stop only work that requires
632	that proof; otherwise admitted bounded construction can continue.
633	
634	### Assertions and observations
635	
636	For an owning obligation r, let Q_r = interpret(r, Gamma, Omega) be its required
637	predicate over a declared case domain Omega. A case includes material inputs,
638	behaviour and environment. Justify this interpretation with its conditions,
639	exceptions and permitted alternatives. A source identifier or digest establishes
640	which text was selected, not that Q_r expresses it faithfully.
641	
642	An assertion targets q_t. State whether it checks Q_r or a narrower condition,
643	and support the implication used by the consuming decision:
644	
645	```text
646	Q_r implies q_t                     q_t is necessary for Q_r.
647	q_t implies Q_r                     q_t is sufficient for Q_r.
648	(q_1 and ... and q_n) implies Q_r    The stated conjunction is sufficient.
649	```
650	
651	These are conditional on Gamma and Omega. A pass on a necessary condition
652	cannot establish Q_r. A collection of assertions needs its own coverage and
653	compatibility argument before its conjunction establishes Q_r. Valid different
654	realisations may satisfy Q_r with different outputs; equality is an oracle only
655	where the obligation requires it.
656	
657	Let pi: Omega → O model the observations available to a checker,
658	and T contained in O × R be the checker's admitted evaluation relation, with R
659	the [core result records](#result-algebra). The following sat and fal abbreviate
660	their satisfied and falsified verdicts about q_t; they add no execution states:
661	
662	```text
663	For every s in Omega:
664	  (pi(s), sat) in T implies q_t(s).
665	  (pi(s), fal) in T implies not q_t(s).
666	```
667	
668	Identify the support and unresolved premises for each claimed direction.
669	Deterministic checking is a functional special case. Human or probabilistic
670	checking may admit different conclusions on the same observations; universal
671	soundness covers every admitted conclusion, not a favourable selected run.
672	A relation may soundly admit both satisfied and indeterminate without always
673	deciding. Its shape supplies no probability distribution. A restricted checker
674	model retains its declared scope; the actual checker and observation acquisition
675	need their own conformance support. An idealised pi does not prove that an
676	instrument or actor acquired the material facts correctly.
677	
678	A reported pass or failure is an observation until the applicable oracle and
679	observation justification support the claimed conclusion. Assess it on the
680	original predicate through the core, retaining actual performance and effects.
681	Insufficient evidence is not a failure of the predicate; an unperformed check
682	is not a performed but undecidable one, and unknown effects stay unknown.
683	
684	A checker claiming always to decide q_t correctly from pi alone requires:
685	
686	```text
687	For all s and s' in Omega:
688	  pi(s) = pi(s') implies q_t(s) = q_t(s').
689	```
690	
691	If equally observed admissible cases disagree on q_t, acquire distinguishing
692	evidence, justify a narrower scope, or return indeterminate on that attempted
693	decision. In a classical set model the condition permits a predicate on the
694	image of pi; it provides neither an executable decision procedure nor a cost
695	bound. Additional independently admissible evidence retains its normal core
696	standing; the limited observation is not permission to erase it.
697	
698	### Parallel assurance and provenance
699	
700	Construction and assertion paths can derive from a common obligation through
701	different refinements. Their assurance depends on each path's justification,
702	not its length or label. Requirement-derived assertions assess the requirement's
703	applicable conditions; refinement-derived assertions assess their more detailed
704	conditions. Neither path automatically covers the other.
705	
706	Assertion provenance identifies the owning obligation, interpretation,
707	assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies that justify the expected
708	predicate. Execution provenance identifies the actual checker, exact subject,
709	applicable environment, inputs, acquired observations and result. Preserve both
710	relations in existing bindings and evidence; execution logs cannot justify an
711	expected answer's derivation. A shared derivation can serve a declared family
712	without a separate document for every test.
713	
714	An implementation-derived assertion can support regression or a stated local
715	property. Repeating that implementation's decision supplies no independent
716	upstream justification. A shorter assertion path can reduce acquisition or
717	execution cost when demonstrated for that path, but it supplies no automatic
718	correctness, coverage or independence.
719	
720	Mutual assurance compares justified constructions or assertions on their stated
721	scope. Agreement admits shared error as well as correctness; disagreement
722	requires diagnosis and does not identify the faulty party by itself. Account for
723	material shared specifications, interpretations, tools, fixtures, observations,
724	copied contributions and other failure causes. Different actors, families or
725	codebases do not establish statistical independence. Repeating an observation
726	does not make it new independent evidence; required authorship independence
727	retains its own conditions.
728	
729	Agreement within an incorrect common model cannot validate that model against
730	the desired outcome. Validation uses the model's declared purpose and material
731	external observations through their owners. Preserve counterexamples and route
732	supported corrections under [Bounded construction](#bounded-construction).
733	The dependence account constrains [risk and assurance selection](#risk-and-assurance-selection).
734	
735	### Risk and assurance selection
736	
737	The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects assurance for the
738	required obligations, material failure consequences and resource limits. Bind
739	coverage, uncertainty and the conditions for action or acceptance. More evidence
740	strengthens a claim only within its applicability and dependence account;
741	test counts or an assumed preference for more checks supply neither. Required
742	safety, authority and acceptance conditions remain applicable to every selected
743	strategy.
744	
745	Quantified assurance requires a declared population or uncertainty model,
746	prior information, likelihoods, shared causes and calibration limits. For a
747	violation event V and evidence event E under Gamma, Bayes' rule gives:
748	
749	```text
750	P(V | E, Gamma) =
751	  P(E | V, Gamma) P(V | Gamma)
752	  / [P(E | V, Gamma) P(V | Gamma)
753	     + P(E | not V, Gamma) P(not V | Gamma)].
754	```
755	
756	The denominator must be nonzero and every used conditional defined. Agreement,
757	disagreement or another observation may be E; its likelihood in faulty and
758	non-faulty conditions matters. The equation supplies no missing prior or
759	likelihood. Its numerical conclusion is bounded by the supporting model and
760	evidence; agreement can fail to increase confidence when shared causes or new
761	information change that model.
762	
763	Let M_i mean that check i misses V under the specified conditions. The exact
764	joint miss probability factors as:
765	
766	```text
767	P(M_1 and ... and M_n | V, Gamma)
768	  = product over i of P(M_i | V, Gamma, M_1, ..., M_(i-1)).
769	```
770	
771	Use the factorisation only on defined conditioning events; handle a
772	zero-probability prefix without inventing a conditional value. Replacing a
773	conditional factor with P(M_i | V, Gamma) requires the relevant conditional
774	independence under that model. One minus the joint miss probability is the
775	chance of at least one detection under those conditions, not the probability
776	that the whole product is correct.
777	
778	Sampled cases or injected defects calibrate only their justified relation to
779	operational failures. Unsupported numerical confidence remains unresolved;
780	qualitative evidence remains usable within governing policy and stated limits.
781	No universal probability threshold or per-test probability estimate is required.
782	The assurance and risk policy constrain cost selection rather than disappearing
783	when a cheaper plan is available.
784	
785	### Change impact and evidence retention
786	
787	Assertion justification explains why a check expresses an obligation. Evidence
788	validity additionally depends on what can affect its behaviour, conclusion or
789	applicability: implementation, libraries, data, instruments, environments and
790	governing assumptions. A requirements-to-test relation alone cannot establish
791	complete change impact.
792	
793	Let Delta change material facts or dependencies, including discovery of an
794	invalid assumption. Let I(Delta) conservatively cover those facts and affected
795	dependents, and D*(t) cover the transitive dependencies material to assertion,
796	execution and reliance on check t. A candidate reassessment selection is:
797	
798	```text
799	S_Delta = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Delta) }.
800	```
801	
802	Excluding a check requires supported dependency coverage and a reason the change
803	cannot invalidate the reused claim. An absent edge proves no non-influence.
804	Unknown impact widens assessment or leaves the dependent assurance unresolved.
805	New obligations and uncovered cases create assessment work even when no existing
806	check covers them; mandatory gates remain applicable. Selection itself produces
807	no execution evidence. The representation need not be an exhaustive graph or a
808	separate ledger.
809	
810	For the new subject and basis, the evidence account combines applicable retained
811	records with actual reassessment, including new obligations and mandatory gates:
812	
813	```text
814	E_new = retain_applicable(E_old, new_subject, new_basis) union E_reassessed.
815	```
816	
817	Retention establishes that claim and scope still apply, assertion and observation
818	bases remain justified, required independence holds, and material dependencies
819	are unchanged or covered by an established preservation relation. The original
820	record keeps its original subject; an applicability relation permits its use
821	for the new claim. A changed digest proves neither invalidity nor equivalence.
822	Changed support reopens affected reliance, not the historical observation.
823	Keep known failures, unresolved coverage and their citations visible until
824	supported repair, reassessment or authorised change of obligation disposes them.
825	
826	A changed requirement revisits dependent expectations under its change authority.
827	A changed refinement revisits its links to the requirement and realisation; a
828	changed realisation revisits affected implementation and integration under the
829	still-applicable obligations. These are semantic dependencies, not fixed file
830	boundaries. Recovery acquires current reality and invalidates affected reliance
831	without erasing valid work or requiring every check to run again. A role,
832	conversation, component or resumption boundary alone is no invalidator.
833	
834	The account's completeness differs from the freshness of every execution.
835	Selection considers impact analysis, acquisition, execution and assessment
836	costs together, separating estimates from measurements. Required assurance,
837	risk policy and mandatory gates constrain that choice; cheap selection cannot
838	leave a required obligation uncovered. Broad or uncertain impact, a changed
839	selection model, a release rule or a missed dependency can justify wider testing.
840	Full-suite execution is available and can still have coverage gaps; no universal
841	cadence or exemption from required gates follows. Failures enter the existing
842	diagnosis and authorised-response relation; obtaining evidence may precede a
843	justified repair.
844	
845	## Workspace and context
846	
847	The workspace is the continuing material state of the construction, including
848	its authoritative requirements, work products and durable records. Material
849	external state is observed through its owning interface. The actor's context is
850	a bounded account acquired from these sources. It is fallible and disposable.
851	Acquisition observes the subject and basis the activation actually binds,
852	including frozen snapshots where selected. Admissible contrary current evidence
853	reopens affected claims through their drift and re-entry rules; it does not
854	silently select a different basis. Current observations correct stale beliefs;
855	they do not grant permission to
856	change a requirement to match the implementation. What exists and what must
857	exist remain different questions on the same truth surface.
858	
859	Acquisition binds the current task, subject, destination constraints, authority
860	and relevant observations. It includes known material dependencies directly or
861	through declared available inputs, and excludes irrelevant material unless
862	needed to establish irrelevance. A rule packet without its current subject is
863	insufficient. A digest without accessible meaning is insufficient. A summary
864	without supported freshness cannot override its owner. Absence from a partial
865	projection, sparse checkout or empty local record is not evidence of absence
866	in the bound subject; acquire its authoritative source or retain indeterminacy.
867	
868	Context fit and adequate attention are different predicates. The execution
869	binding declares the material resource envelope and measurement boundary;
870	counted bytes or tokens establish fit only for the context actually covered by
871	that measurement. Actual use establishes whether the actor applies sufficient
872	relevant material to the selected task under those conditions. Fitting a
873	representation does not establish attention adequacy, and a successful task
874	does not measure unobserved context. No universal attention score follows.
875	
876	An observation binds its source and observation time or version. Where the
877	subject may change between observation and effect, the binding supplies the
878	material freshness or concurrency condition: re-observe, compare a revision,
879	use a protected snapshot or return uncertainty. No universal isolation scheme
880	follows. The selected operation cannot assume a stale read is still current.
881	
882	The cycle is acquisition from current state, a bounded authorised operation,
883	observation of its result, and acquisition for the next operation. Results use
884	[the result algebra](#result-algebra). The cycle can stop after any operation
885	without inventing completion. Private context can be discarded between cycles;
886	resumption reconstructs sufficient context from the continuing workspace and
887	authoritative inputs. It neither erases progress nor requires a transcript of
888	every earlier activation.
889	
890	For reuse, apply [Change impact and evidence retention](#change-impact-and-evidence-retention)

The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects assurance for the
required obligations, material failure consequences and resource limits. Bind
coverage, uncertainty and the conditions for action or acceptance. More evidence
strengthens a claim only within its applicability and dependence account;
test counts or an assumed preference for more checks supply neither. Required
safety, authority and acceptance conditions remain applicable to every selected
strategy.

Quantified assurance requires a declared population or uncertainty model,
prior information, likelihoods, shared causes and calibration limits. For a
violation event V and evidence event E under Gamma, Bayes' rule gives:

```text
P(V | E, Gamma) =
  P(E | V, Gamma) P(V | Gamma)
  / [P(E | V, Gamma) P(V | Gamma)
     + P(E | not V, Gamma) P(not V | Gamma)].
```

The denominator must be nonzero and every used conditional defined. Agreement,
disagreement or another observation may be E; its likelihood in faulty and
non-faulty conditions matters. The equation supplies no missing prior or
likelihood. Its numerical conclusion is bounded by the supporting model and
evidence; agreement can fail to increase confidence when shared causes or new
information change that model.

Let M_i mean that check i misses V under the specified conditions. The exact
joint miss probability factors as:

```text
P(M_1 and ... and M_n | V, Gamma)
  = product over i of P(M_i | V, Gamma, M_1, ..., M_(i-1)).
```

Use the factorisation only on defined conditioning events; handle a
zero-probability prefix without inventing a conditional value. Replacing a
conditional factor with P(M_i | V, Gamma) requires the relevant conditional
independence under that model. One minus the joint miss probability is the
chance of at least one detection under those conditions, not the probability
that the whole product is correct.

Sampled cases or injected defects calibrate only their justified relation to
operational failures. Unsupported numerical confidence remains unresolved;
qualitative evidence remains usable within governing policy and stated limits.
No universal probability threshold or per-test probability estimate is required.
The assurance and risk policy constrain cost selection rather than disappearing
when a cheaper plan is available.

### Change impact and evidence retention

Assertion justification explains why a check expresses an obligation. Evidence
validity additionally depends on what can affect its behaviour, conclusion or
applicability: implementation, libraries, data, instruments, environments and
governing assumptions. A requirements-to-test relation alone cannot establish
complete change impact.

Let Delta change material facts or dependencies, including discovery of an
invalid assumption. Let I(Delta) conservatively cover those facts and affected
dependents, and D*(t) cover the transitive dependencies material to assertion,
execution and reliance on check t. A candidate reassessment selection is:

```text
S_Delta = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Delta) }.
```

Excluding a check requires supported dependency coverage and a reason the change
cannot invalidate the reused claim. An absent edge proves no non-influence.
Unknown impact widens assessment or leaves the dependent assurance unresolved.
New obligations and uncovered cases create assessment work even when no existing
check covers them; mandatory gates remain applicable. Selection itself produces
no execution evidence. The representation need not be an exhaustive graph or a
separate ledger.

For the new subject and basis, the evidence account combines applicable retained
records with actual reassessment, including new obligations and mandatory gates:

```text
E_new = retain_applicable(E_old, new_subject, new_basis) union E_reassessed.
```

Retention establishes that claim and scope still apply, assertion and observation
bases remain justified, required independence holds, and material dependencies
are unchanged or covered by an established preservation relation. The original
record keeps its original subject; an applicability relation permits its use
for the new claim. A changed digest proves neither invalidity nor equivalence.
Changed support reopens affected reliance, not the historical observation.
Keep known failures, unresolved coverage and their citations visible until
supported repair, reassessment or authorised change of obligation disposes them.

A changed requirement revisits dependent expectations under its change authority.
A changed refinement revisits its links to the requirement and realisation; a
changed realisation revisits affected implementation and integration under the
still-applicable obligations. These are semantic dependencies, not fixed file
boundaries. Recovery acquires current reality and invalidates affected reliance
without erasing valid work or requiring every check to run again. A role,
conversation, component or resumption boundary alone is no invalidator.

The account's completeness differs from the freshness of every execution.
Selection considers impact analysis, acquisition, execution and assessment
costs together, separating estimates from measurements. Required assurance,
risk policy and mandatory gates constrain that choice; cheap selection cannot
leave a required obligation uncovered. Broad or uncertain impact, a changed
selection model, a release rule or a missed dependency can justify wider testing.
Full-suite execution is available and can still have coverage gaps; no universal
cadence or exemption from required gates follows. Failures enter the existing
diagnosis and authorised-response relation; obtaining evidence may precede a
justified repair.

## Workspace and context

The workspace is the continuing material state of the construction, including
its authoritative requirements, work products and durable records. Material
external state is observed through its owning interface. The actor's context is
a bounded account acquired from these sources. It is fallible and disposable.
Acquisition observes the subject and basis the activation actually binds,
including frozen snapshots where selected. Admissible contrary current evidence
reopens affected claims through their drift and re-entry rules; it does not
silently select a different basis. Current observations correct stale beliefs;
they do not grant permission to
change a requirement to match the implementation. What exists and what must
exist remain different questions on the same truth surface.

Acquisition binds the current task, subject, destination constraints, authority
and relevant observations. It includes known material dependencies directly or
through declared available inputs, and excludes irrelevant material unless
needed to establish irrelevance. A rule packet without its current subject is
insufficient. A digest without accessible meaning is insufficient. A summary
without supported freshness cannot override its owner. Absence from a partial
projection, sparse checkout or empty local record is not evidence of absence
in the bound subject; acquire its authoritative source or retain indeterminacy.

Context fit and adequate attention are different predicates. The execution
binding declares the material resource envelope and measurement boundary;
counted bytes or tokens establish fit only for the context actually covered by
that measurement. Actual use establishes whether the actor applies sufficient
relevant material to the selected task under those conditions. Fitting a
representation does not establish attention adequacy, and a successful task
does not measure unobserved context. No universal attention score follows.

An observation binds its source and observation time or version. Where the
subject may change between observation and effect, the binding supplies the
material freshness or concurrency condition: re-observe, compare a revision,
use a protected snapshot or return uncertainty. No universal isolation scheme
follows. The selected operation cannot assume a stale read is still current.

The cycle is acquisition from current state, a bounded authorised operation,
observation of its result, and acquisition for the next operation. Results use
[the result algebra](#result-algebra). The cycle can stop after any operation
without inventing completion. Private context can be discarded between cycles;
resumption reconstructs sufficient context from the continuing workspace and
authoritative inputs. It neither erases progress nor requires a transcript of
every earlier activation.

For reuse, apply [Change impact and evidence retention](#change-impact-and-evidence-retention)

1359	### Quantified assurance

1361	Risk model. The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects the required
1362	assurance for the stated risk, obligations and resource limits. That
1363	selection identifies material failure consequences, coverage and
1364	uncertainty, and the conditions for action or acceptance. Additional
1365	evidence can strengthen a claim only within its applicability and
1366	dependence account; neither a test count nor an assumed preference for more checks
1367	substitutes for that account (P6, P5).

1370	uncertainty being modelled, prior information, likelihoods, shared causes
1371	and calibration limits. For a specified violation event V and evidence
1372	event E:

1374	```text

1376	  P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ)

1380	The denominator must be nonzero. E can include agreement, disagreement or other
1381	observations; its likelihood under both faulty and non-faulty conditions
1382	matters. The formula supplies no missing likelihood or prior, and a
1383	numerical posterior is no stronger than its model and evidence.

1386	conditions. The joint miss probability factors exactly by conditional

1391	  = product over i of P(M_i | V, Γ, M_1, ..., M_(i-1)).

1395	prefixes are handled without inventing a conditional value. Replacing

1406	remain usable within the governing policy. No universal probability

1411	### Change impact and evidence reuse
1412	
1413	Assertion justification and evidence validity are related but distinct
1414	dependency relations. The former explains why a check expresses an
1415	obligation. The latter identifies what can affect the check's behaviour,
1416	conclusion or applicability: implementation, shared libraries, data,
1417	instruments, environments and governing assumptions. A
1418	requirements-to-test link alone is not a complete impact model (P3, P6).
1419	
1420	Let Δ be a change to material facts or dependencies, including a newly
1421	discovered invalid assumption. Let `I(Δ)`, the impact cover, conservatively cover the changed
1422	facts and their affected dependents. For each check t, let `D*(t)` cover
1423	the transitive dependencies material to its assertion, execution and use
1424	of evidence. A candidate selection is:
1425	
1426	```text
1427	S_Δ = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Δ) }.
1428	```
1429	
1430	The representation of these dependencies is the tenant's choice; no
1431	exhaustive graph database is required. Excluding a check requires
1432	supported coverage of its material dependencies and a reason the change
1433	cannot invalidate the intended reused claim; an absent edge is not
1434	evidence of non-influence. Unknown impact widens reassessment or leaves
1435	the dependent assurance unresolved. New obligations or cases create

1437	gate, an assessment that the governing policy requires irrespective of

1439	(P5, P6).

1441	For a new subject and basis, let `E_old` be the existing evidence records,
1442	`E_reassessed` the evidence newly produced by reassessment, and `E_new`
1443	the resulting account. Reassessment includes the checks selected in
1444	`S_Δ`, the assessment of new obligations and the applicable mandatory
1445	gates. Selection alone produces no execution evidence; failed and

1447

1450	```
1451	
1452	Retention establishes the material validity conditions on the new
1453	subject: the claim and its scope still apply, its assertion and
1454	observation basis remain justified, and the affected dependencies are
1455	unchanged or covered by an established preservation relation. The
1456	original evidence keeps its original subject; a new applicability
1457	relation permits its use. A changed hash alone establishes neither
1458	invalidity nor equivalence. Known failures, unresolved coverage and their
1459	citations remain visible until a supported repair, a reassessment or an

1461	
1462	If a governing requirement changes, dependent expectations may need
1463	authorised revision as well as new execution. A correction in a

1467	still-applicable obligations. These are semantic dependency boundaries,
1468	not file or directory boundaries. Recovery reacquires current reality and

1471	
1472	The governing assurance can be established from applicable retained

### Assurance relations

The relations below connect construction to the assertions, observations
and evidence that support claims about it. They are the shared owner for
the preservation, assertion, provenance, quantified-assurance, reuse and
formal-representation obligations in this corpus; ACTIVATION §1, §4, §5 and §7, EVALUATION §1 and §3,
ASSURANCE §3, §10, §11 and §14, RELEASE §8 and §9, SPEC_METHOD §4 and
the a_c interpretation apply them and state no second relation (P6). They are law
carried from the common assurance requirement. A tenant chooses its
representation and execution within these obligations. The notation
states proof obligations; writing an implication does not discharge it.

Foundation to law. This family, assurance relations, covers the six
subsections that follow. Its instance premises are: (a) a construction
with the governing basis bound at intake under ACTIVATION §1 and the
material assumptions, together written Γ here; (b) a declared domain Ω of cases, each with the inputs,
behaviour and environment material to an obligation; (c) a checker with
declared observations and an admitted evaluation relation. They are
conditions of the situations the family governs, not commitments.

| Premises, with standing | Consequence that follows | Rule in this member that states it | Added domain or policy choice, and its owner | Pillar |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P4a (independent), P1 (independent), P6 (independent); instance premise a | By P4a a composite exists only where each boundary is compatible, by P1 a relation written down is not thereby discharged, and by P6 a preservation claim is a claim on evidence, so each claimed step states its domains, relation and property, the implication is a proof obligation, and a relation covering completion alone says nothing about refusal, failure, interruption or unknown effects | [Preservation through construction](#preservation-through-construction) | the adequacy relation and bound of an approximate step: the owner of the step's law | 3, 4, 9 |
| P4a (independent), P2 (independent), P6 (independent); instance premise a | By P4a the composite's property follows only through compatible boundaries, by P2 the final property matters only through its connection to Z, and by P6 that connection is argued, not assumed, so an end-to-end argument establishes the initial condition, each step's premises, compatibility at each boundary and the connection to Z, and preservation is distinct from progress and termination | [Preservation through construction](#preservation-through-construction) | the composition law for concurrency, branches and external effects: the owner of the construction's design | 3, 4, 7 |
| P1 (independent), P6 (independent), P5 (derived from P0 and P6, with P0's open-world premise); instance premises a, b | By P1 an assertion's predicate is distinct from the obligation it is derived from, by P6 passing a necessary condition establishes no more than that condition, and by P5 a conjunction's coverage is a claim of its own, so each assertion states whether its predicate is the obligation, a necessary condition or part of a sufficient conjunction, conditional on Γ and Ω | [Assertions and observation](#assertions-and-observation) | the declared domain Ω and the interpretation: the owner of the obligation and the assessor's activation | 6, 9 |
